1. To form one closed loop, the copies must join crosswise: \(P\) to \(Q'\) and \(Q\) to \(P'\). Otherwise the copy would have to coincide with the original.
2. If \(R\) is the rotation taking the first copy to the second, then
   \[
   R(Q-P)=P-Q=-(Q-P).
   \]
   Hence \(R\) must be a \(180^\circ\) rotation about the midpoint of \(PQ\).
